input: inorder and postorder are equal-length arrays of n distinct safe integers describing valid inorder and postorder traversals of the same binary tree. Empty traversals are accepted. All collections are ordinary finite dense arrays/lists, not subclasses, proxies, sparse arrays or accessor-backed collections. Node fields, where present, are ordinary data fields. Every individual collection length and computed allocation dimension/count fits [0,4294967295]; explicitly stated padded sizes and heap child-index arithmetic must also fit the declared exact numeric domain. No concurrent mutation or built-in monkey-patching is permitted. Preconditions are not runtime-checked; allocation/resource capacity and actual completion still require qualification. JavaScript integer inputs are primitive safe-integer Number, excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt; separately declared probabilities are finite primitive Number.
return: A fresh TreeNode root reconstructing the unique tree, or None/null for empty traversals. Each node has val, left and right data fields, with absent children None/null.
mutation_aliasing: Input arrays remain unchanged. Exactly n fresh helper-defined TreeNode objects form the output; no output node aliases an input or a preexisting node. The Solution instance retains no state.
numeric: Values are compared only for exact equality. Traversal indices stay in [-1,n-1]. Valid unique traversals guarantee a parent is popped before a left child is attached. All integer inputs and integer intermediates (apart from opaque Python identity keys) remain in [-9007199254740991,9007199254740991]; no bitwise coercion is used.
complexity: O(n + 1) time; O(h + 1) auxiliary stack space plus O(n) new output-node storage, where h is reconstructed tree height. Reverse postorder visits root/right/left, and each node is pushed/popped at most once. Bounds count ordinary built-in allocations and assume bounded-word arithmetic, constant-time indexing, amortized append/pop, and stated hash/sort guarantees where relevant.
